notes.text: This undated manuscript leaf bears the authorial 7 and thin secondary foliation 23. It continues a characterization of closed subsets compatible with a conical germ by cylindrical data upstairs and closed data in Y, then defines compatibility between a cylindrical germ at X0 and a conical germ near Y. The lower homothety draft and diagram are cancelled. These are transcription-level descriptions; they are not a verification of the corollary or of all compatibility assertions.

The image formula is retained literally with the underbrace attached to Im(tilde X′ par tilde X→X), although its left end lies beneath the right half of m rather than at the full left edge. The lower annotation has a closure bar over X′\(Y∩X′), with a second brace identifying Y∩X′ as Y′. No grouping or hypothesis is silently supplied to the source. The intended image–closure equality is the limited target of N03.

Independent counterexample to the underbrace equality only. Let S=(0,1]×[0,1], B=(0,1]×{0}, Y=[0,1], and f:B→Y be f(a,0)=a. Form the quotient X=S amalg_B Y and let q denote the quotient map from S disjoint-union Y. Choose tilde X′=S, Y′=Y and X′=X. These chosen parts are closed in their own ambient spaces; S has the evident product cylinder near B, and f maps B into Y′. The image q(S) is X with the class of 0∈Y omitted: no point of B maps to 0, while all positive basepoints do. Meanwhile X′\Y is precisely the positive-height cylinder. Every neighbourhood U of the class of 0 has q^{-1}(U)∩Y open in Y and containing 0, so it contains some a>0. The same quotient class is q(a,0), hence q^{-1}(U)∩S is open in S and contains (a,0). Product topology then forces (a,t) in that preimage for some t>0. Thus every neighbourhood of 0 meets the positive-height part; the same statement is immediate at positive basepoints, and positive-height points already belong to that part. Consequently closure_X(X′\Y)=X, whereas Im(tilde X′→X)=q(S)=X\{0}. The written identification of that image with the closure is false under these general quotient assumptions.

Scope of N03: the union identity X′=q(S)∪Y′ remains true in the same example, since X is the quotient of S disjoint-union Y. The example therefore refutes only the underbrace’s image–closure equality. It neither refutes nor proves the full claimed correspondence with canonical cylindrical subsets. No theorem about the entire corollary is certified by this report, and no source symbol is changed in response to this calculation.

Revision stages are preserved locally: the old underlined strict[.] compatible avec is crossed; cônique strict is a live raised replacement with strict underlined; the entire lower article–structure cônique clause and its inserted purement/germe de candidate are crossed. The raised candidate attaches after the article, not before it. Only soient, not the following baseline des parties cylindriques de, is raised in the lower condition. Because E i.e. falls within the global cancellation, the retained live lower wording ends with de; no completion is supplied.

Literal wording includes une germe de and the abbreviation il f et. s. (no point after f; points after et and s). Cônique is accented where an independent mark is present, while the occurrence before calligraphic T in P12 is conique without an independent accent. The page’s abbreviations and lack of final points are not normalized.

Both slanted margins are distinct from upright body spillover. The upper reads au lieu de “compatible” il est plus parlant de dire “transversal”, with paired source ticks and a single underline under transversal. The lower reads donc stable par E-homothéties par λ∈[0,1]. Rotated cropping is for inspection only; the transcription keeps them as margins. Extra upright E/curves near the upper margin and the main cancellations near the lower margin are excluded, not duplicated.

Bars are decided locally. In the lower live condition the first T has one cap and is plain; the first and third E have detached-looking high marks that leave bar/plain uncertainty, bar preferred. In the diagram, top E has its three ordinary arms with no separately identified fourth bar. Middle/lower E each have three arms in total, including the high detached-looking arm; plain E is preferred there with a bar alternative. Each T0 and the final T in the diagram has one cap only. The final lower-right X0 has a separate dot, unlike the upper definition’s X0, and is retained as dotted rather than harmonized.

Diagram accounting: eight principal formula objects, three horizontal ≃ relations and three vertical cups; no fourth cup or arrowhead is supplied. The product factors use thin serif I, unlike the heavy inserted I in P14. The entire lower draft is cancelled by nine long diagonal strokes, including the leftmost across E i.e.; the small old group has additional local crossing and now favors E-subscript-zero followed by I, with E∩T as an alternative. Tikz-cd typesets the formula cells, with end-picture strokes recording the global cancellation; running text E i.e. is separately transcribed as deleted. Normal diagram spacing is used and no text glyphs are redrawn as paths.

Inspection record: original whole image once and each supplied native half once, then saved P01–P21 crops inspected once; the failed P21 delivery produced no viewed image and was redelivered successfully. P22 completes the clipped upper f of fermées and was inspected once. P23 was intended as an ascender completion but overlaps almost entirely with the already inspected P16 frame; it is retained as an inadvertent overlapping strip, with no new source decision and no claim of previously unexamined ink. No further crop was made. P16 plus P17 already provide that shared context. No OCR, external research, compilation or other-page access was used.

Scoped refinement of the underbrace claim for the full cylinder used in N03. More generally, let S=A×[0,1], B=A×{0}, f:B→Y be continuous, and X=S amalg_B Y. The positive-height part S\B is dense in S, so continuity gives q(S)⊂closure_X(q(S\B)); conversely q(S\B)⊂q(S), hence their closures coincide. The preimage of q(S) under the quotient S disjoint-union Y→X is S disjoint-union f(B). Thus q(S) is closed in X exactly when f(B) is closed in Y, directly by the quotient closed-set criterion. Since q(S\B)=X\Y, the equality q(S)=closure_X(X\Y) holds exactly when f(B) is closed in Y. In N03 f(B)=(0,1] is not closed in [0,1]. This refinement concerns the full-cylinder image identity only; no general theorem about every compatible subspace is inferred.

The eight-object diagram, three equivalences, three cups and nine diagonals were counted twice. No new crop was required. The fixed first/second readings remain unchanged; the mathematical check events are unchanged.
